chunks: Al-Hakim Abu Muhammad Ja'far ibn Nu'aym ibn Shadhan narrated to us; his uncle Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Shadhan narrated to him; Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee' narrated to us, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him).

I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him) about the Qunut in the Fajr and Witr prayers; he said: Before bowing. And I asked him about drinking Al-Fuqah (a type of beer); he disliked it with strong dislike. And I asked him about praying in a garment with designs; he disliked what has images/portraits in it. And I asked him about a young girl whom her father marries off, then he dies while she is still young, and she matures before her husband consummates the marriage with her; is the marriage valid for her, or is the decision left to her? He said: The marriage of her father is valid for her.

He (peace be upon him) said: Abu Ja'far said: Nothing breaks the ablution except what comes out from the two exits which God has placed in you, or he said: the two which God has favored you with. And I asked him about the prayer in Mecca and Medina; is it shortened or complete? He said: Shorten it as long as you do not resolve to stay for ten days. And I asked him about the veil of women in the presence of eunuchs; he said: They used to enter upon the daughters of Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and they did not cover themselves.

And I asked him about the mother of a child (concubine); is it permissible for her to uncover her head among men? He said: She must cover herself. And I asked him about vessels of gold and silver; he disliked them. I said to him: Some of our companions narrated that Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) had a mirror plated with silver. He said: No, praise be to God; it only had a silver ring and it is with me. And he said: Al-Abbas, meaning his brother, when he was circumcised, a cane was made for him plated with silver, like what is made for children, its shaft being worth about ten dirhams; so Abu al-Hasan ordered it to be broken.

And I asked him about a man who has a young slave girl and kisses her; is she permissible for his son? He said: With lust? I said: Yes. He said: No, he has not left anything (i.e., done the major act). If he kisses her with lust. Then he (peace be upon him) said spontaneously: If he undressed her and looked at her with lust, she becomes forbidden for his father and his son. I said: If he looks at her body? He said: If he looks at her private parts.

And I asked him about the age limit of a young girl, such that if she does not reach it, men are not required to observe her waiting period (Istibra'). He said: If she has not reached puberty, she is observed for one month. I said: What if she is seven years old or thereabouts, from those who do not get pregnant? He said: She is young and it does not harm you if you do not observe her waiting period. I said: What is between that and nine years old? He said: Yes, nine years old.

And I asked him about a woman who was tried by drinking Nabidh (a drink) and got drunk, so she married herself to a man while drunk, then she regained consciousness and denied it, then she thought it was binding on her, so she abstained from him, then she stayed with the man upon that marriage; is it valid for her, or is the marriage invalid due to the drunkenness and the husband has no claim over her? He said: If she stays with him after regaining consciousness, that is her pleasure. I said: Is that marriage valid for her? He said: Yes.

And I asked him about a slave girl owned by two men, so they freed her, and she has an absent brother and she is a virgin; is it permissible for either of them to marry her, or is it not permissible except by the command of her brother? He said: Yes, it is permissible for him to marry her. I said: Then he can marry her if he wishes? He said: Yes.

And he said to me: Have a good opinion of God, for God, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am with the good opinion of My believing servant towards Me; if [he thinks] good, then [I give him] good, and if [he thinks] evil, then [I give him] evil.' And he said regarding the Imams: They are truthful scholars, understood [by God], and spoken to [by God].
He said: I wrote to Al-Rida (peace be upon him): People differ regarding Al-Rabaysa (a type of fish); what do you order me to do regarding it? He wrote back: There is no harm with it.

key_terms.أُمُّ الْوَلَد: Concubine who bears her master's child
key_terms.الاسْتِبْرَاء: Waiting period to check for pregnancy
key_terms.الْفُقَاع: A type of beer or fermented drink

ai.seo_question: What are the legal rulings of Imam Al-Rida regarding marriage, prayer, and purity?
ai.summary: This extensive hadith from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* demonstrates Imam al-Rida’s (AS) comprehensive jurisprudence, addressing both ritual purity and social customs with precision. It notably clarifies the timing of Qunut before Ruku, the prohibition of beer (al-Fuqa'), and the validity of paternal marriage contracts for young girls, while also correcting misconceptions regarding the use of silver vessels by the Ahl al-Bayt. The narration concludes with a spiritual maxim linking divine proximity to the believer's expectation of God, reflecting the Shia emphasis on combining legal rigor with theological optimism.
